xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4434: Overdeck Anywhere P0: /ws/terminal app-level heartbeat (ping/pong control frames)

plan.title: Overdeck Anywhere P0: /ws/terminal app-level heartbeat (ping/pong control frames)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Proxies such as Cloudflare close a WebSocket after ~100 s without traffic. /ws/rpc and /events/stream already send 15 s heartbeats, but /ws/terminal sends nothing while a terminal is idle, so idle terminals behind such proxies drop, and the server cannot detect half-open terminal sockets.
narratives.Proposal: Add src/dashboard/server/ws-terminal-heartbeat.ts: for connections that opt in with ?heartbeat=1, send the control frame \u0000{"type":"ping"} every 20 s from connection onward; any inbound message resets a missed counter and two consecutive silent intervals call ws.terminate(). ws-terminal.ts drops {"type":"ping"}/{"type":"pong"} client messages at its single ws.on('message') entry point so they never reach the PTY. XTerminal.tsx (after extracting its control-frame parse into components/terminal/terminalControlFrames.ts to stay under its file-size cap) opts in with heartbeat=1, answers pings with {"type":"pong"}, and stops writing unknown parsed control frames into xterm. Three docs describe the shipped heartbeat.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No ws.ping() protocol-level pings and no change to /ws/rpc, /ws/voice, /ws/autopreso or /events/stream heartbeats
- No server reply to a client ping; it is only dropped
- No heartbeat or heartbeat termination for connections without heartbeat=1, and no forced reload of stale bundles
- No change to the upgrade/auth block of ws-terminal.ts, ws-auth.ts or route-scopes.ts
- No change to terminalReconnectPolicy.ts; a terminated socket reconnects through the existing path
- No raise of any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt cap
- No edit to the separate OKF knowledge bundle repo
- No special handling of suspended background tabs: they stop answering pings, are terminated after 40-60 s and reconnect on resume; this is intended

autoDecisions.summary: The heartbeat is opt-in via the ?heartbeat=1 query parameter, which XTerminal always sends
autoDecisions.rationale: Current XTerminal writes unrecognized \u0000 control frames into xterm and never pongs; after pan reload, open tabs reconnect with the stale bundle (StaleBuildChip only prompts), so an unconditional heartbeat would paint ping text every 20 s and terminate those terminals every 40-60 s. A query param (not an attach field) is needed because attach is read only after a respawn wait of up to 95 s.

autoDecisions.summary: Ping/pong client messages are dropped once at the ws.on('message') entry point instead of in each of the four handlers
autoDecisions.rationale: All four handlers (pre-attach, Herdr, hub-join, local) fall through to a PTY/bridge write; one filter before dispatch covers them all and keeps pongs out of the pre-attach message/byte budget, while parseControlMessage is still widened as the issue asks.

autoDecisions.summary: The client drops parsed control frames of unknown type but keeps passing malformed \u0000 messages through to xterm
autoDecisions.rationale: Prevents future control frames from rendering as text without risking loss of a live PTY chunk that happens to start with NUL.

autoDecisions.summary: Docs scope covers DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md plus DASHBOARD-AUTH.md and configuration/remote-access.mdx
autoDecisions.rationale: The latter two currently say /ws/terminal has no heartbeat and list PAN-4434 as pending; leaving them would contradict shipped code.

items.title: Add the /ws/terminal heartbeat module with fake-timer tests

expected_outputs: ws-terminal-heartbeat.test.ts passes all six named cases

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/server/ws-terminal-heartbeat.ts exactly as PRD W1 shows: constants TERMINAL_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS=20_000, TERMINAL_HEARTBEAT_MAX_MISSED=2, TERMINAL_HEARTBEAT_QUERY_PARAM='heartbeat', wantsTerminalHeartbeat(url), and startTerminalHeartbeat(ws, sendPing) implementing the D-5 tick rule (missed resets on any inbound message, terminate at 2 consecutive silent ticks, otherwise send ping; clear on close/error). It must not import ws-terminal.ts. Add ws-terminal-heartbeat.test.ts with the six named cases from PRD W1 using vi.useFakeTimers() and a FakeSocket extends EventEmitter with terminate = vi.fn().

items.title: Given fake timers and a socket that receives a message before each tick, when 60 000 ms elapse, then sendPing is called 3 times and terminate is never called

Given a silent tick followed by an inbound message, when two more ticks pass with the second silent, then terminate is not called; when a fourth consecutive silent tick passes, then terminate is called exactly once
Given no inbound messages, when 40 000 ms elapse, then terminate is called once and when 120 000 ms elapse the timer has stopped so terminate stays at one call

Given a sendPing that answers each ping with a pong message, when 600 000 ms of fake time elapse, then 30 pings are recorded, no gap between outbound pings exceeds 20 000 ms, and terminate is never called
When the socket emits close or error, then no further ping is sent and wantsTerminalHeartbeat returns true only for heartbeat=1
Wire the opt-in heartbeat into ws-terminal.ts and drop ping/pong input

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/server/ws-terminal.ts follow PRD W2: import startTerminalHeartbeat and wantsTerminalHeartbeat, widen ClientControlMessage with ping and pong, make parseControlMessage return ping/pong, start the heartbeat right after the 'WebSocket connected for session' log only when wantsTerminalHeartbeat(url) is true (sending sendControl(ws, { type: 'ping' })), and drop ping/pong at the top of the single ws.on('message') listener before messageHandler or the pre-attach buffer. Do not edit the four handlers or the upgrade block. Add ws-terminal-heartbeat-wiring.test.ts with a real loopback server and mocked node-pty, tmux and resolveTerminalAttachTarget as PRD W2 specifies. The test also spies startTerminalHeartbeat (case 3) and fires the fake pty's stored onExit callback in afterEach so the 5 s ptyDiagInterval never leaks.

items.title: Given a connection to /ws/terminal?session=x&heartbeat=1 that has attached and sent ready, when the client sends {"type":"pong"}, {"type":"ping"} and "x", then the mocked pty.write receives "x" and never receives either heartbeat message
Given a pong sent before the attach message, when the client then attaches and sends "y", then pty.write receives "y" and the pong is never written or buffered as input

Given startTerminalHeartbeat wrapped in a vi.fn spy, when a client connects with heartbeat=1, then the spy is called once before the client sends attach; when a client connects without the parameter and attaches, then the spy is called zero times
